newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cognac region fears rise in spirits tax.
newsitem.headline: French cognac region fears rise in spirits tax.

text.p: Mayors and cognac producers demonstrated on Monday in the southwestern French town of Angouleme against a planned 17.1 percent tax increase on spirits.
About 200 people took part in the demonstration outside the offices of the local prefect (government representative).
Cognac producers fear the higher tax, which will be debated in parliament on Tuesday, would be fatal for an industry already suffering in a weak domestic economic climate.
Throughout the day, town halls remained closed across the Cognac region where mayors have refused to send wine harvest accounts to tax authorities for the past month.

Global cognac sales have fallen 60 percent in the last 15 years and employment in trading houses slid 10 percent in the last decade. In 1993, a tax increase of 16 percent was imposed on spirits, which are more more heavily taxed in France than wine or beer.
